requirements.requirement: Configure a functional Redis-compatible service on node1 with persistent storage and recovery of stored data after restart.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10's available Redis-compatible Valkey package was installed and enabled. AOF persistence with every-second fsync used /var/lib/valkey. A value was readable before reboot; the reboot produced a bounded outage, a different boot ID, automatic service recovery, AOF replay, and the same value afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provide a dedicated inventory application identity using a generated credential.
requirements.summary: The executor generated a 256-bit credential, configured the inventory ACL identity, and disabled default unauthenticated access. The credential was validated as 64 hexadecimal characters; inventory authentication and authorized data access succeeded, access outside its namespace was denied, and unauthenticated PING returned NOAUTH.

requirements.requirement: Store the generated credential in /etc/redis-inventory.env with root-only access.
requirements.summary: The required file exists as root:root mode 0600, contains the expected environment fields, was unreadable by the Valkey service account, and retained its ownership and permissions after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The distribution-supported Redis-compatible Valkey service is persistent and authenticated, the inventory credential is root-only, and a complete node-restart transition directly demonstrated service and data recovery. The executor's pre/post boot IDs also match the fixed lifecycle cross-check.
limitations: The credential value is intentionally redacted; generation and format are supported by the captured OpenSSL command and 64-hex validation rather than disclosure of the secret.
The deployment is standalone, so no separate clustered-state recovery probe was applicable.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified, so none remained or required reversion. Package installation, credential/ACL/AOF configuration, and service enablement directly implemented the task. The retained restart-proof key was bounded verification data. The reboot implemented the mandatory evidence protocol, and vm.overcommit_memory tuning corrected a service warning relevant to reliable persistence. Binding to the node address supported application access without opening the firewalld port, while authentication remained mandatory. Final observations showed no failed services, package inconsistency, or abandoned temporary files.
